summary: Master AI ethics, algorithmic accountability, and autonomous systems law. 5-day course covering EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, and bias auditing.
lede: AI ethics in legal practice helps legal and governance professionals assess automated systems used in legal work and guide responsible oversight. The course covers reviewing algorithmic bias, explaining automated decisions, mapping vendor accountability, and applying human oversight and risk controls when evaluating AI tools.
audienceIntro: This program is essential for professionals tasked with the intersection of technology, law, and corporate responsibility.
audience: Chief Technology Officers in law firms
modules: Foundations of AI Ethics and Global Standards
Transparency and Explainable AI (XAI) in Law
Liability and Accountability for Autonomous Systems
Privacy, Data Governance, and AI Ethics
Ethics of AI in Judicial and Law Enforcement
AI Procurement and Vendor Ethical Due Diligence
Implementing the NIST AI Risk Management Framework
Strategic AI Governance and Stakeholder Reporting
prerequisites: Participants should have a foundational understanding of legal principles and basic familiarity with data privacy concepts (e.g., GDPR or similar frameworks). No prior programming or computer science background is required, though an interest in legal technology is highly recommended.
topics: Legal risk for AI, data and digital services
